parsed.rationale: Sinus rhythm at about 70 bpm with narrow QRS complexes; the ST segments are essentially isoelectric in every lead, with no contiguous ST elevation meeting STEMI criteria, and the prominent but symmetric T waves in V2–V4 alone don't establish an anterior MI on this tracing, though in a patient with symptoms they could be hyperacute T waves and a repeat ECG would be warranted.
